bibl.title: Associative priming and conflict differentially affect two processes underlying cognitive control: Evidence from reaching behavior

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Thus, by directly evaluating the influence of associative-priming confounds, the present study revealed the strongest evidence to date that decision behavior in tasks involving conflict is fundamentally structured by the functioning of two dissociable processes.

span.label: congruency sequence effect in the Stroop task
span.quote: Thus, a CSE was not observed on confound-minimized trials, but a CSE was observed on set repeat trials, which featured substantial associative-priming effects.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: We therefore presented 45 adult participants with a reach-tracking version of the Stroop task that featured both confound-minimized and confound-laden trials.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Coactivation of competing responses on incongruent trials raises the response threshold, lengthening motoric stopping and thus slowing initiation, with the raised threshold carrying over into the next trial
span.quote: On this view, the coactivation of competing responses on incongruent trials results in heightened response thresholds, with longer periods of motoric stopping and, consequently, slower initiation times.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Overlap between the current and previous trial's stimulus-response features either helps or hinders the formation of the appropriate stimulus-response pair, and that facilitation or interference shows up as more or less reach curvature
span.quote: According to this interpretation, associative-priming effects influence performance by either impeding or facilitating an individual’s ability to form the appropriate stimulus–response pair, resulting in reach movements that feature more or less curvature.

span.label: The study used only a reach-tracking task, so it cannot say whether button-press response times would show the same pattern.
span.quote: Given that the present study did not involve both button-press and reach-tracking versions of the same task, it is unclear whether button-press response times in the task would reveal the same pattern of response time effects observed with reaching behavior.

span.label: The task did not separate stimulus-level from response-level conflict and did not control contingency-learning effects; the authors call for tasks that do.
span.quote: Hand-tracking tasks should therefore be developed to investigate the effects of stimulusand responselevel conflict in tasks that control for both associative-priming and contingency-learning effects.

span.label: every individual trial was VISUALLY INSPECTED and those where the automatic threshold missed part of the movement were identified
span.note: eliminates: that the movement measures are corrupted by an automatic threshold that mis-segments the reaching trajectory
span.quote: Each individual trial was visually inspected, as in previous work (e.g., Song & Nakayama, 2007); for trials in which the default threshold clearly missed part of the movement or included substantial movement back to the starting point, the thresholds were adjusted manually to ensure that the movement ended at the selected target.

span.label: a practice block of 24 Stroop trials preceded the experiment
span.note: eliminates: that early Stroop performance reflects unfamiliarity rather than conflict
span.quote: practice block of 24 trials of the Stroop task before beginning the experiment.

span.label: associative priming
span.quote: The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, including conflict adaptation and associative priming

span.label: conflict adaptation
span.quote: The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, including conflict adaptation and associative priming

span.label: CSE
span.quote: This pattern of effects is often referred to as the congruency sequence effect (CSE), because the size of the congruency effect (the performance difference between congruent and incongruent trials) is smaller on trials preceded by an incongruent trial (iC and iI trials) than on trials preceded by a congruent trial

span.label: initiation times
span.quote: Initiation times revealed main effects of previous and current congruency on both confound-minimized and confound-laden trials, consistent with the claim that initiation times can be used to target the functioning of the threshold adjustment process

span.label: reach curvatures
span.quote: Conversely, reach curvatures exhibited a clear sensitivity to associative-priming effects, revealing a congruency sequence effect on confound-laden but not on confound-minimized trials

span.label: **PRIMING AS THE CONFOUND RATHER THAN THE PHENOMENON, WHICH THIS CORPUS HAS ALMOST NONE OF:** `The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, INCLUDING CONFLICT ADAPTATION AND ASSOCIATIVE PRIMING.` Two accounts of one effect, and **the priming account needs no control process at all** - if the current trial repeats the previous trial's stimulus and response, the pairing was already formed. So a CSE is not evidence for cognitive control until the overlap is removed. Every other record I have tagged treats priming as the object of study; here it is the alternative explanation
span.quote: The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, including conflict adaptation and associative priming

span.label: **AND THE AUTHORS SAY PLAINLY THAT THE EARLIER WORK - INCLUDING THEIR OWN - LEAVES THE QUESTION OPEN:** `Consequently, the extent to which the observed patterns reflected the proposed processes OR ASSOCIATIVE-PRIMING CONFOUNDS REMAINED UNCLEAR.` The preceding sentence - that earlier tasks did not control for those confounds - is fused in the staged text and cannot be quoted. **This is a whole literature's results placed in doubt by the people who produced some of them**, and it is what motivates the design rather than a limitation conceded at the end
span.quote: Consequently, the extent to which the observed patterns reflected the proposed processes or associative-priming confounds remained unclear

span.label: **THE DISSOCIATION IS PRODUCED BY A CONTROL RATHER THAN BY A MANIPULATION, WHICH IS THE RARER AND STRONGER FORM:** initiation times showed the effect `on BOTH confound-minimized and confound-laden trials`; reach curvatures showed it `on confound-laden BUT NOT on confound-minimized trials`. **Nothing was added to the design - something was taken away, and one of the two measures lost its effect with it.** A dissociation obtained by subtraction cannot be explained by whatever the added factor also did, which is the usual objection to the added-manipulation kind
span.quote: Conversely, reach curvatures exhibited a clear sensitivity to associative-priming effects, revealing a congruency sequence effect on confound-laden but not on confound-minimized trials

span.label: **AND THE STROOP TASK APPEARS HERE AS APPARATUS, NOT AS SUBJECT:** a three-response, reach-tracking version, 84 years after Stroop 1935, used to ask about trial-to-trial control rather than about interference. **The corpus now holds the founding paper and a paper that treats it as equipment** - and the pair is worth more than either, because it shows what happens to a paradigm when it stops being a finding and becomes a method
span.quote: We therefore presented 45 adult participants with a reach-tracking version of the Stroop task that featured both confound-minimized and confound-laden trials

span.label: extends → Erb & Marcovitch (2018a, 2018b); Erb et al. (2016, 2018b)
span.quote: In contrast to previous hand-tracking studies (Erb & Marcovitch, 2018a, 2018b; Erb et al., 2016; Erb et al., 2018b), the task used in the present study allowed for a direct comparison of confound-minimized and confound-laden trials.

span.label: replicates → Schmidt & De Houwer (2011); Weissman, Jiang, & Egner (2014)
span.quote: This finding is consistent with a number of previous studies that have failed to observe a CSE in the Stroop task after controlling for alternative explanations (e.g., Schmidt & De Houwer, 2011; Weissman, Jiang, & Egner, 2014).

span.label: contradicts → Scherbaum, Dshemuchadse, Fischer, and Goschke (2010, Exp. 2)
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER STIMULUS REPETITIONS ARE EXCLUDED. 'Scherbaum, Dshemuchadse, Fischer, and Goschke (2010, Exp. 2) OBSERVED A SIGNIFICANT CSE in participants' hand movements in a mouse-tracking version of the Simon task, EVEN AFTER STIMULUS REPETITIONS WERE EXCLUDED FROM THE ANALYSIS, whereas th[is study]...' The disagreement is between two analyses of the same confound, not between two claims about the effect. Q-444.
span.quote: For example, Scherbaum, Dshemuchadse, Fischer, and Goschke (2010, Exp. 2) observed a significant CSE in participants’ hand movements in a mouse-tracking version of the Simon task, even after stimulus repetitions were excluded from the analysis, whereas the present study did not reveal a CSE in reach curvatures in confound-minimized trials.

span.label: associative priming —causes→ CSE
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — **ONE OF TWO RIVAL ACCOUNTS, AND `has been attributed to` IS THE HEDGE, INSIDE THE QUOTE.** This edge is not the paper's finding - it is the position the paper tests. Weight 0.7 because the sentence reports an attribution in the literature rather than a result here, and because this paper's own data cut both ways: the curvature CSE disappears when the priming confound is removed (so priming was carrying it) while the initiation-time CSE does not (so priming was not). **A corpus that recorded only the surviving effect would lose the reason anyone doubted it.**
span.quote: The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, including conflict adaptation and associative priming

span.label: conflict adaptation —causes→ CSE
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — THE OTHER RIVAL, on the same sentence and at the same weight, deliberately. The two edges are symmetrical because the quote is symmetrical - it lists both without choosing. **Recording one and not the other would make the corpus take a side the sentence does not take**, and the paper's contribution is precisely that it separates them empirically rather than arguing for one. The separation lives in the third sense.
span.quote: The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, including conflict adaptation and associative priming

span.label: associative priming —contrasted-with→ conflict adaptation
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THIS IS THE EDGE THE PAPER IS ABOUT**, and it is the only one of the three that carries the paper's own claim rather than the literature's. The two accounts predict the same effect and differ in whether a control process is needed at all - one is top-down regulation, the other is feature repetition requiring nothing. Weight 0.9: the contrast is explicit in the quote and the whole design exists to resolve it.
span.quote: The CSE has been at the center of recent debates surrounding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cognitive control and has been attributed to a range of factors, including conflict adaptation and associative priming

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: The data were analyzed using a series of 2 (set: change vs. repeat) × 2 (response: change vs. repeat) × 2 (previous congruency: c vs. i) × 2 (current congruency: C vs. I) repeated measures analyses of variance (ANOVAs).

span.label: F-test
span.quote: The results of this analysis revealed a significantly larger CSE in curvatures in set repeat than in confound-minimized trials, F(1, 44) = 4.18, p = .047, ηp 2 = .09.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: The results of this analysis revealed a significantly larger CSE in curvatures in set repeat than in confound-minimized trials, F(1, 44) = 4.18, p = .047, ηp 2 = .09.

span.label: effect size (partial eta squared)
span.quote: The results of this analysis revealed a significantly larger CSE in curvatures in set repeat than in confound-minimized trials, F(1, 44) = 4.18, p = .047, ηp 2 = .09.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: Forty-five adults participated in the study for course credit (M = 19.7 years, SD = 3.0; 26 females, 18 males, one nonbinary).

span.label: mean
span.quote: Forty-five adults participated in the study for course credit (M = 19.7 years, SD = 3.0; 26 females, 18 males, one nonbinary).

span.label: standard error
span.quote: for the measures (a) initiation time, (b) curvature, (c) movement time, (d) response time, and (e) error rate. Error bars display standard errors

span.label: Initiation times showed main effects of both current and previous congruency whether or not associative-priming confounds were present, supporting a threshold adjustment process that is not reducible to priming.
span.quote: Thus, initiation times revealed the same pattern of effects (cC < iC < cI < iI) regardless of the presence of associative-priming effects.

span.label: Reach curvature showed a congruency sequence effect only on confound-laden set repeat trials and not on confound-minimized trials, indicating that the curvature CSE is driven by associative priming rather than conflict adaptation.
span.quote: Thus, a CSE was not observed on confound-minimized trials, but a CSE was observed on set repeat trials, which featured substantial associative-priming effects.

span.label: The size of the curvature CSE was itself reliably larger on set repeat than on confound-minimized trials.
span.quote: The results of this analysis revealed a significantly larger CSE in curvatures in set repeat than in confound-minimized trials, F(1, 44) = 4.18, p = .047, ηp 2 = .09.

span.label: On confound-minimized trials reach curvature responded only to current congruency, with no carry-over from the previous trial and no interaction.
span.quote: Reach curvatures on confound-minimized trials revealed a significant main effect of current congruency, but no main effect of previous congruency or interaction between previous and current congruency.

span.label: Error rates on confound-minimized trials tracked current congruency alone, mirroring the curvature pattern.
span.quote: Error rates on confound-minimized trials revealed a significant main effect of current congruency, but no main effect of previous congruency or interaction between previous and current congruency.

span.label: congruency sequence effect (CSE)
span.quote: This pattern of effects is often referred to as the congruency sequence effect (CSE), because the size of the congruency effect (the performance difference between congruent and incongruent trials) is smaller on trials preceded by an incongruent trial (iC and iI trials) than on trials preceded by a congruent trial

span.label: curvature
span.quote: Curvature was defined as the maximum point of deviation, in centimeters, divided by the length of the line from the start to the end point of the movement, in centimeters

span.label: initiation time / movement time
span.quote: Initiation time was calculated as the time elapsed between stimulus onset and movement onset; movement time was calculated as the time elapsed between movement onset and response completion

span.label: confound-minimized trials
span.quote: This task design allowed for a subset of confound-minimized trials to occur, in which the stimulus and response features of the current trial did not overlap with those of the previous trial.

span.label: current congruency (congruent vs. incongruent)
span.quote: The data were analyzed using a series of 2 (set: change vs. repeat) × 2 (response: change vs. repeat) × 2 (previous congruency: c vs. i) × 2 (current congruency: C vs. I) repeated measures analyses of variance (ANOVAs).

span.label: previous-trial congruency
span.quote: Initiation times on confound-minimized trials revealed significant main effects of previous congruency and current congruency, but no interaction between the two.

span.label: presence of associative-priming confounds (confound-minimized vs. set repeat trials)
span.term: presence of associative-priming confounds (confound-minimized vs. set repeat trials)
span.quote: This task design allowed for a subset of confound-minimized trials to occur, in which the stimulus and response features of the current trial did not overlap with those of the previous trial.

span.label: initiation time
span.quote: Initiation time was calculated as the time elapsed between stimulus onset and movement onset; movement time was calculated as the time elapsed between movement onset and response completion

span.label: reach curvature
span.quote: Curvature was defined as the maximum point of deviation, in centimeters, divided by the length of the line from the start to the end point of the movement, in centimeters

span.label: error rate
span.quote: Error rates on confound-minimized trials revealed a significant main effect of current congruency, but no main effect of previous congruency or interaction between previous and current congruency.

span.label: exclusion of inaccurate trials and the trial following an error
span.term: exclusion of inaccurate trials and the trial following an error
span.quote: resulting in 6% of the experimental trials being excluded from analysis for the measures of initiation time, curvature, movement time, and response time.

span.label: handedness and visual acuity of participants
span.term: handedness and visual acuity of participants
span.quote: All participants were right-handed with normal or corrected-to-normal visual acuity.

span.label: 45 — number of adult participants tested in the reach-tracking Stroop task
span.quote: We therefore presented 45 adult participants with a reach-tracking version of the Stroop task that featured both confound-minimized and confound-laden trials.

span.label: M = 19.7 years, SD = 3.0 — mean and standard deviation of participant age in the final sample
span.quote: Forty-five adults participated in the study for course credit (M = 19.7 years, SD = 3.0; 26 females, 18 males, one nonbinary).

span.label: F(1, 44) = 4.18, p = .047, ηp 2 = .09 — test of whether the curvature CSE was larger on set repeat than on confound-minimized trials
span.quote: The results of this analysis revealed a significantly larger CSE in curvatures in set repeat than in confound-minimized trials, F(1, 44) = 4.18, p = .047, ηp 2 = .09.

span.label: 6% — share of experimental trials discarded (errors plus post-error trials) before analysing the timing and curvature measures
span.quote: resulting in 6% of the experimental trials being excluded from analysis for the measures of initiation time, curvature, movement time, and response time.

span.label: 3.4% (SD = 3.0%) — average per-participant share of trials whose movement-onset threshold had to be adjusted by hand
span.quote: An average of 3.4% (SD = 3.0%) of experimental trials were adjusted manually for each participant.

span.label: approximately 160 Hz — sampling rate of the electromagnetic motion-tracking system recording the reach
span.quote: Reach movements and response selections were measured at a rate of approximately 160 Hz with an electromagnetic position and orientation recording system

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.3758/s13423-019-01576-y.
